counts_basis: Counts describe this repository's development tree (unreleased changes, uncommitted on the distribution/public-release branch when counted) on 2026-11-14, except python_tests and python_test_files, which are the 0.1.1 pytest collection counts (commit 45b2a0a) because the development-tree count was still changing; on 2026-11-14 the development tree collected 2034 tests in 59 modules (a collection count, not a run). native_tests counts #[test] functions in native/windows-receiver/src. failure_guides counts the guides adapt explain --list shows (GUIDES in failure_guide.py, including 33 native receiver reason codes and 19 native receiver command outcomes); 0.1.1 has none. physical_phones_with_saved_evidence counts the two phones of the pre-release record; the 2026-11-14 record (0.1.1 smoke passes and native receiver sessions, one Windows 11 PC) adds an Android 16 tablet and does not say whether its Android 13 and Android 17 phones are the same units. No count is a pass rate. counts_0_1_1 holds the 0.1.1 values of the counts that differ.

functional_areas.capability: Official Google Platform-Tools acquisition, digest verification, safe extraction, version gate, and user-scope setup.
functional_areas.evidence: Tested offline across mock/fixture scenarios in tests/test_setup_download.py.
functional_areas.boundary: Fresh installer acceptance is not established on both host OSes; repository checksum fallback is documented. On Linux, setup needs an x86-64 host. Without --yes outside a terminal, setup stops before changing anything. Development tree: setup refuses on macOS, registers its own earlier install on PATH without downloading again, and exits non-zero when aborted or failed.

functional_areas.capability: Toolchain detection, port 5037 shared-daemon safety check, USB driver/udev permission checks, and interactive Next action menu.
functional_areas.evidence: Windows 11 host observations on pre-release builds, and doctor --json with 0.1.1 on a Windows 11 host on 2026-11-14; offline diagnostics in tests/test_doctor.py. The Linux path is offline-tested only, and the development tree's doctor changes are offline-tested only.
functional_areas.boundary: Device Manager opens for manual driver work on Windows; does not install OEM drivers automatically. On Linux provides udev commands. 0.1.1 treats every Linux host as Debian and reads the udev rules file from a source checkout only. Development tree: Debian-family, other Linux and macOS (unsupported) are told apart, the rules file ships in the wheel, a distribution-packaged adb at or above 34.0.0 is a warning, and running as root or Administrator prints a warning.

functional_areas.entry: adapt adb; adapt pair; adapt connect; adapt devices
functional_areas.capability: Exact transport targeting (-s), daemon preflight, bounded wireless pairing/connection with port separation, and guarded shell execution.
functional_areas.evidence: Bounded USB/Wi-Fi and routed ADB observations on pre-release builds; with 0.1.1 on 2026-11-14, one USB and two wireless-debugging transports; see docs/validation.md. Raw device receipts are not published.
functional_areas.boundary: Pairing alone is not a connected transport. Android 11+ requires separate pairing and connection ports. Android 10 requires legacy USB-first workflow. Without a named target, adapt adb uses the only ready device.
generic_examples: adapt adb -- -s SERIAL shell getprop ro.build.version.release

functional_areas.capability: Original fading ASCII logo banner, 9 functional command category screens, Home/Back/Page navigation, and basic terminal fallback.
functional_areas.evidence: Interactive verification on Windows terminal; VT sequence handling and --no-redraw append-only mode tested.
functional_areas.boundary: Rapid remains an integrated option within ADAPT, not a separate fork. Redraw can be disabled for screen readers.

functional_areas.entry: adapt help-me; adapt explain; adapt tips; adapt guide
functional_areas.capability: Full command inventory, 76 authored help topics with generic examples, contextual guidance tips, saved user tip preferences, and (development tree) failure guidance: a Why/Try/More block after errors, a failure object in JSON and MCP errors, and offline lookup with adapt explain.
functional_areas.evidence: Offline-tested in tests/test_help_system.py, tests/test_hints.py, tests/test_cli_help.py, tests/test_failure_guide.py, tests/test_failure_report.py and tests/test_failure_cli.py.
functional_areas.boundary: Tips are automatically silenced when stdout is not a TTY or when --json is passed to keep machine output clean. Failure guidance runs nothing. Errors and refused or failed results get a specific guide where ADAPT tagged them and the generic internal.unclassified guide otherwise; the dex receiver-* commands are the exception (their refusals carry no guidance, and receiver-status explains a receiver reason code in its own last_failure block). Failure guidance has offline tests only and has not been seen on a real failure.

functional_areas.capability: Curated catalog of 16 Android tools across 6 workflow goals; local PATH detection, upstream source tracking, and ROM build guidance.
functional_areas.evidence: Offline catalog inspection tested in tests/test_tool_catalog.py.
functional_areas.boundary: Catalog discovery observes PATH; does not verify provenance, build AOSP trees, or install prerequisites automatically.
generic_examples: adapt tools plan lineage-build --device devicename --branch branchname

functional_areas.capability: Pinned acquisition of scrcpy v5.0.1, SHA-256 archive validation, zip-slip / tar-bomb protections, and install receipt tracking.
functional_areas.evidence: Unit and integration testing of archive extraction and hash verification in tests/test_scrcpy_install.py.
functional_areas.boundary: Archive extraction and hash verification are tested offline against fixtures; no download of the real upstream archive is recorded, and native Debian validation is outstanding (docs/scrcpy.md).

functional_areas.capability: Batch inspection of host environment, catalog detection, confirmed setup of supported tools, and optional exact-device checks.
functional_areas.evidence: Tested across multiple dry-run and execution scenarios in tests/test_everything.py.
functional_areas.boundary: Only 2 tools (platform-tools, scrcpy) support automatic acquisition; 14 other catalog tools receive guidance. Zero automatic device mutations.

functional_areas.capability: Mapping 9 API baselines (API 29-37, Android 10-17 including 12L) to supported features (USB, wireless pairing, Wi-Fi 2.0, legacy TCP, DeX).
functional_areas.evidence: Physical phone verification on the Android 13 (API 33) and Android 17 (API 37) phones on pre-release builds; android capabilities with 0.1.1 on an API 33 phone, an API 37 phone and an API 36 tablet on 2026-11-14; remaining API levels covered by offline matrix fixtures.
functional_areas.boundary: API level reports OS eligibility, not hardware/OEM certification. Presence of an API does not guarantee OEM feature support.

functional_areas.capability: Passive observation of ADB and fastboot endpoints, SU candidates, custom ROM properties (Lineage, crDroid), and bootloader lock state.
functional_areas.evidence: Tested across various property dumps and mock outputs in tests/test_device_state.py. detect inspect read values with 0.1.1 on three Samsung devices on 2026-11-14.
functional_areas.boundary: Zero transitions: no reboot, flashing, or unlocking. Absence of SU binary does not prove a device is stock unrooted. Samsung Download mode is not fastboot.

functional_areas.capability: 13 inspected settings across Global, System, and Secure tables plus read-only maker-layer detection (Pixel, Samsung One UI, other); 14 profiles (fast-ui, touches, desktop-testing, stay-awake, layout-debug, lifecycle-stress, performance-capture, battery-doze, rtl-large-font, accessibility-display, input-visualization, network-degraded, background-restricted, debugger-attach) over settings, debug.* properties and command pairs with conflict-aware schema 2 snapshots (schema 1 still restores); a profile listing with per-device eligibility; an offline 176-entry catalog; a page-size check.
functional_areas.evidence: Live stay-awake inspection on the API 33 and API 37 phones on pre-release builds; with 0.1.1 on 2026-11-14, one touches apply and restore on an API 33 phone read back as expected; snapshot creation, atomic write, and rollback tested in tests/test_dev_options.py; the 14 profiles, property and command-pair entries, detection, the catalog and the page-size check are offline-tested only (tests/test_dev_options_v2.py, test_dev_profiles.py, test_dev_detect.py, test_dev_catalog.py, test_safety_dev_options.py).
functional_areas.boundary: Mutates only allowlisted keys, properties and commands; no raw Binder calls and no SystemProperties poke; network-cutting profiles are refused over wireless adb. Restores only if current device value matches snapshot target or original; flags external conflicts. Only one apply and restore cycle that changed a value is recorded (touches, API 33); other profiles, rollback and conflicts are offline-tested only.
generic_examples: adapt dev-options apply --profile stay-awake -s SERIAL --snapshot stay-awake.json

functional_areas.capability: Package installation status, version code, and debuggability validation; debug app inspection and command planning; build terminology.
functional_areas.evidence: Tested across app validation, debug configuration, and build mode fixtures in tests/test_development.py.
functional_areas.boundary: Validates installed state via pm/dumpsys. Does not attach debugger, launch processes, verify cryptographic APK signatures, or infer R8.
generic_examples: adapt app validate -s SERIAL --package com.example.app --expect-debuggable false --json

functional_areas.capability: Bounded app-UID logcat extraction (main/crash buffers), fixed-tag system diagnostics (window, dex, print), and vendor logging documentation.
functional_areas.evidence: Live DeX system-log capture on the API 33 phone on pre-release builds; log capture and tag filtering tested in tests/test_diagnostics.py.
functional_areas.boundary: Read-only bounded extraction (max 500 lines). Never runs logcat -c. Logs may contain private data. Empty logcat is not proof of no crash.
generic_examples: adapt logs capture -s SERIAL --package com.example.app --lines 200 --output app-logs.json
adapt logs diagnostic -s SERIAL --topic window --minutes 2 --output window.json

functional_areas.capability: Inspect secondary display eligibility, apply recoverable desktop/freeform options, and launch apps in isolated virtual displays via scrcpy.
functional_areas.evidence: Virtual display planning, parameter validation, and scrcpy command construction tested in tests/test_desktop.py. desktop inspect read values with 0.1.1 on three Samsung devices on 2026-11-14.
functional_areas.boundary: Virtual displays test Android multi-window app behavior; they do not prove Samsung DeX or desktop window manager decorations.

functional_areas.capability: Logical display discovery, dual-mirroring with scrcpy, temporary Java bridge probe, experimental PC receiver session lifecycle supervision, and (development tree) start, status and stop of a user-built native receiver.
functional_areas.evidence: Live dual-mirroring, display inspection, and native Windows receiver prototype (an earlier source revision) verified on the Android 13 (API 33) phone on pre-release builds; 1 controlled reconnect passed. On 2026-11-14, all on one Windows 11 PC with one Wi-Fi adapter and admission restricted by device name: the 0.1.1 receiver source held one session of about four minutes with an Android 13 phone; the development-tree receiver with audio on held a session of about 90 seconds with an Android 13 phone, one of about 48 minutes with an Android 17 phone (One UI 9) and a short one with an Android 16 tablet (One UI 8); on the Android 17 phone the owner confirmed real mouse and keyboard input and audible sound and judged the audio quality great (one listener, one session). The receiver-* commands were run against the real receiver without a phone, and receiver-status and receiver-stop with the Android 17 phone and the Android 16 tablet streaming. Development-tree dex inspect confirmed DeX from display flags on the Android 17 phone and the Android 16 tablet, one wireless session each; dex plan-dual-mirror produced a plan on the phone but nothing was launched.
functional_areas.boundary: Native receiver is experimental source, manually built and outside the Python package. Display targeting requires fresh runtime evidence; no display ID is fixed. ADAPT activation was denied by firmware on the one phone tried and has not been observed succeeding. The receiver admits any phone by default; the optional name and peer ID restrictions are not authentication. With 0.1.1, dex inspect recognises DeX state only from the desktopmode service and reports unknown on One UI 8 and 9, which have no such service. The development tree also parses one Android 13 firmware's form (offline-tested only) and, only when the service is absent, confirms DeX from display flags; wired and standalone DeX, and scrcpy capturing a flag-confirmed display, are not observed. dex pc-probe was refused on One UI 9 during a wireless DeX session. Real input and audible sound on the receiver were confirmed on one phone only; reconnects on the current source, open admission with a device connecting, failure reason codes, a release build and sessions over about 48 minutes are not observed.
generic_examples: adapt dex pc-start -s SERIAL --method loopback --snapshot dex-session.json --yes

functional_areas.capability: Explicit remote worker inspection, strict OpenSSH option enforcement (BatchMode, strict host checking), and MCP-over-SSH configuration output.
functional_areas.evidence: Command line generation, PowerShell encoding, and strict option validation tested in tests/test_ssh_worker.py.
functional_areas.boundary: Architecture guidance for hypervisors (Proxmox, VMware, Hyper-V, VirtualBox, XCP-ng); no hypervisor API adapters or live SSH acceptance. Development tree: failure reports carry a fixed reason code and hint.
generic_examples: adapt ssh run android-worker --operation inspect --device SERIAL --json

functional_areas.capability: 13 leaf operations for peer discovery, TCP port probing, pairing/connecting over tailnet, guarded remote ADB commands, and worker integration.
functional_areas.evidence: Local peer status parsing, pairing verification on the API 37 phone, and mock suite in tests/test_tailscale_mode.py.
functional_areas.boundary: An online peer does not prove an active ADB listener. On the tested Samsung firmware service.adb.tls.port was empty, creating a verification gap for the strict TLS check. No complete direct Tailscale run exists; a private routed VPN path that carried ADB commands is not Tailscale evidence.
generic_examples: adapt tailscale adb --peer PHONE_PEER --port CONNECT_PORT -- shell getprop ro.product.model

functional_areas.capability: Structured plan generation for the focused testing cycle: check -> prepare -> reproduce -> capture -> restore.
functional_areas.evidence: Plan validation and JSON schema structure tested in tests/test_development.py.
functional_areas.boundary: Explain-only plan. Generates commands but executes none; not an automated journey runner or session rollback supervisor.
generic_examples: adapt rapid plan -s SERIAL --package com.example.app --session-dir test-session --json

functional_areas.capability: Local stdio Model Context Protocol (MCP) server offering 38 tools (24 read-only, 14 mutating) with exact transport filtering and bounded outputs, short server instructions, 13 build-test loop tools (app launch, stop and state, log marks with a since window, test runs, Developer Options apply and restore with ADAPT-owned snapshots, runtime permissions, tapping and waiting by text), a human title plus read-only/destructive/idempotent/open-world annotations on every tool, static adapt:// resources and a help tool; and (development tree) the adapt agent commands: a Markdown or JSON primer for any AI agent with a shell, built from the live command tree and tool classification, a client table with config printing, a diff-first install with backups, an Agent Skill, an AGENTS.md block and a server check.
functional_areas.evidence: Tested across server lifecycle, schema conformance, and access policies in tests/test_mcp.py, tests/test_mcp_contract.py, and tests/test_mcp_access.py; the primer, the server instructions and the tool titles and annotations in tests/test_agent_guide.py; the 13 build-test loop tools (schemas, access policy, argv shapes, bounded output, the test_run and test_status lifecycle and the snapshot rules) in tests/test_mcp_agent_tools.py against faked adb output; the resources and the help tool in tests/test_mcp_resources.py; the client table, config, install, restore, skill, AGENTS.md block and verify in tests/test_agent_clients.py, tests/test_agent_install.py and tests/test_agent_skill.py, all against temporary folders. With 0.1.1 on 2026-11-14, read-only --device sessions driven by a scripted client against three Samsung devices listed 18 tools, returned list_devices, device_info and screenshot, and refused tap; list_devices labelled the two wireless-debugging transports usb. No AI client was involved.
functional_areas.boundary: No live external AI client registration or live MCP-over-SSH exercised, no AI client has been observed reading the server instructions, the resources or the primer, no client registration written by adapt agent install has been live-checked (clients with third-party or unstated facts are print-only), MCP prompts are not implemented, and no tool that acts on the phone recorded against a real device (the 13 build-test loop tools have offline tests only). DeX MCP input currently lacks explicit display targeting (assumes phone display). Development tree: the 14 tools that act on the phone require an explicit device unless the server was started with exactly one --device; read-only tools use the only ready device when none is named; list_devices reads the transport label from the serial (tcp, local or usb); error results carry a failure object, with new error codes adb_command_refused and unsafe_shared_server. These development-tree changes have offline tests only. In 0.1.1 the five tools that then existed to act on the phone also use the only ready device.
generic_examples: codex mcp add adapt -- adapt mcp --read-only
